files.content:
"use client";

import React from 'react';
import { DownOutlined } from '@ant-design/icons';
import { Button, Dropdown, Space } from 'antd';

const App: React.FC = () => (
  <Space>
    <Dropdown.Button icon={<DownOutlined />} menu={{ items: [] }}>
      Submit
    </Dropdown.Button>
    <Dropdown.Button icon={<DownOutlined />} placement="top" menu={{ items: [] }}>
      Submit
    </Dropdown.Button>
    <Space.Compact>
      <Button type="primary">Submit</Button>
      <Dropdown menu={{ items: [] }}>
        <Button type="primary" icon={<DownOutlined />} />
      </Dropdown>
    </Space.Compact>
    <Space.Compact>
      <Button>Submit</Button>
      <Dropdown menu={{ items: [] }} placement="top">
        <Button icon={<DownOutlined />} />
      </Dropdown>
    </Space.Compact>
  </Space>
);

export default App;

documentation:
# Ant Design Dropdown

Open a menu of actions from a trigger control.

## Installation

- Complete MIT example compositions using the pinned antd npm package.
- Ant Design supplies component styling at runtime. Add application validation and persistence when wiring form controls to your backend.

- Copy every returned file and preserve the MIT licence notice.
- Render the returned preview.tsx example, or integrate the example into your existing provider.
